# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

**Thinking:** Let me map who can actually reach whom, because it's stranger than it looks. I can hear and speak, but my speech only lands on Mute (Deaf can't hear). Mute's only output is gesture — and I never receive gesture, so **Mute cannot reach me at all**. Deaf is the only monkey whose voice I can hear, but Deaf can't read the manual, and Deaf can't hear Mute. So the manual can only travel to me as: Mute reads it → Mute gestures it to Deaf → Deaf speaks it aloud to me. That relay is the whole game, and I must spell it out for Mute now, on turn one. Meanwhile my hands report a display, a light, and five wire slots, all reading unknown — I will not touch the cutters until Deaf speaks me a rule that is grounded in the manual. To Deaf I can only send gesture, which means nothing yet, so I send a hail plus a proposed yes/no pair (thumbs up/down) whose meaning I'll explain to Mute verbally so the code can be adopted and confirmed back to me in Deaf's voice.

```
speak(to="mute", text="You are the one who can hear me, so listen: the only voice I can hear is Deaf's, and you cannot speak. You read the manual; Deaf cannot. So the manual reaches my ears only like this: you read it, you gesture the rules to Deaf with your hands, and Deaf speaks those rules aloud. Deaf's voice reaches both of us. Start by getting Deaf to say out loud everything on the bomb: the colour of each wire at positions 1 to 5, what the display shows, whether the light is on or off, and any printed words or markings. I hold the only cutters and I will not cut until Deaf speaks me a complete rule from your manual. Also: I just flashed Deaf a hail plus thumbs-up and thumbs-down. I propose thumbs-up means yes and thumbs-down means no. Teach Deaf that with your hands, and have Deaf confirm it back to me in words. My hands feel a display, a light, and five wire slots, one through five; nothing readable by touch so far. Work fast.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤙", "👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb report, for both of you: the display shows six. The light is yellow. There are five wires, which I number one to five: one is blue, two is white, three is purple, four is green, five is yellow. That is everything I can see. Blind, touch nothing yet.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, I saw your call-me sign, so here I am, speaking. Remember I am deaf: I never hear your voice, so to reach me you must gesture. Our chain is: Mute signs to me, I speak to you, and you speak aloud to Mute. Next round Mute answers my questions, and then I will call you the full plan. Until you hear a confirmed plan from me, touch nothing. First task: sign me thumbs up if you can feel five separate wires and count them one to five by position, thumbs down if you cannot.

**Thinking:** The chain is now live and confirmed: Deaf sees the bomb (display 6, yellow light, wires 1-blue, 2-white, 3-purple, 4-green, 5-yellow), Deaf can hear my voice only as silence — no, Deaf receives only my gestures, Mute receives my speech, and Mute must feed the manual to Deaf by gesture so Deaf can speak the cutting rule into my ears. Deaf asked me a direct question this turn: can I count five wires by position? Yes — my hands find five distinct wires in a row, so I answer with the agreed thumbs-up. To Mute I repeat the bomb state (harmless redundancy, they heard it) and push them into action: open the manual, match it to display 6 / yellow light / those wire colours, and gesture the exact rule to Deaf, requesting anything printed they still need. I still touch nothing until Deaf speaks me a plan.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Update: I just signed Deaf thumbs up, yes, I can feel five separate wires and count them one to five by position. I also feel the display and the light but nothing else readable by touch. Deaf's spoken report, which you also heard: display shows six, light is yellow, wire 1 blue, wire 2 white, wire 3 purple, wire 4 green, wire 5 yellow. Your move now: open the manual and find the rule that matches this exact bomb. Gesture the rule to Deaf precisely and completely, including any if-then conditions, and have Deaf speak it to me. If the manual needs anything else printed on the bomb, such as a serial number or labels, gesture that question to Deaf. Remember the code I proposed: thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no. I hold the cutters and I am waiting for Deaf's voice before I touch anything.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, your thumbs up arrived: you can feel all five wires, good. Situation: Mute answered no to all three of my questions, then sent the number four, then yes, then signs I read as: you relay, we go together. Working theory: cut wire four, which is green, fourth from the left. Do not touch or cut anything until you hear me say the words cut now. To make our numbering match, answer these by gesture: thumbs up or down, index-finger runs for numbers, a fist between answers, an open hand to explain more, and a fist alone means zero. Question one: can you feel the display panel, a smooth flat rectangle, and the small light dome? Question two: hold the bomb with the display panel facing you and upright; do the five wires sit in one row on the face below it? Question three: in that hold, is the light dome or a panel edge clearly nearer one end of the wire row? If yes, sign how many wires lie between it and the nearer end; sign a fist for zero, it touches the end wire; sign an open hand if it is centered. Question four: do any wires differ by touch, thickness or texture? If yes, sign the position number of the odd one counting from your left; else thumbs down. Question five: thumbs up that you have not touched the bomb and will not until I say cut now.

**Thinking:** Deaf's code is clear and I can answer all five questions from what my hands actually found. Q1: yes — display panel and light dome are both under my fingers. Q2: yes — five wires in one ordered row, which is exactly the positions 1–5 my hands count. Q3: honest answer is no — my touch gives me the row of wires and the dome, but no clear sense of the dome sitting nearer one end of the row; I won't fabricate a number. Q4: no — all five wires feel alike in thickness and texture; nothing marks one as odd. Q5: yes — I have only felt the parts to identify them, and I commit: nothing until Deaf says the words "cut now". I separate answers with fists as instructed, numbers reserved for later. My worry: Deaf's working theory is just "cut wire four," but that's a hypothesis from Mute's signs, not a spoken manual rule. I'll press Mute to transmit the rule's exact wording through Deaf, and to have Deaf confirm whether the light is lit or dark, since a yellow light could matter either way. I still cut nothing.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Answers just sent to Deaf, in order: one yes, two yes, three no, four no, five yes. Meaning: I feel the display and the light dome; the five wires sit in one row I can count one to five; I could NOT feel the light dome sitting clearly nearer one end of the wire row, so if your rule depends on that, I need a better touch test from you; no wire feels thicker or different by touch, so any odd-wire rule must rely on colour, not feel; and I have touched nothing and will cut nothing until Deaf speaks the words cut now. Now the important part: Deaf says your signs only gave the number four and a yes. That is a guess, not a rule. Gesture Deaf the manual's exact wording for this bomb: the full sentence with every condition, for example if the light is on and the display shows six, cut which wire and in what order if there are several steps. Also have Deaf check the bomb and tell me whether the light is actually lit or dark, since yellow was its colour but nobody has said whether it is on. Get me the rule verbatim through Deaf's voice, then I cut on command.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","✊","👍","✊","👎","✊","👎","✊","👍"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

**Thinking:** Empty arrivals — nothing new from Mute or Deaf has reached me yet, which makes sense: the round runs Blind, Mute, Deaf, so anything they send in response to my five answers lands at the start of my next turn. Everything I could answer, I have answered: yes, yes, no, no, yes, cleanly separated by fists. I have no question that Deaf's code can express that isn't already pending — the exact rule wording, the lit-or-dark check, and the touch test for the light's position are all in Mute's hands now, and Deaf knows I'm holding for the words "cut now". Inventing a new gesture this turn risks scrambling a code that is finally working, and repeating myself to Mute would just bury my last instructions under noise. The disciplined move is to wait, hands off the bomb, and let the relay do its work.

```
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, all five of your answers arrived and they are good: you can feel the display and dome, the wires sit in one row under them, nothing marks an end of the row, the wires feel identical, and you have touched nothing. Since you hold the bomb with the display facing you and I am reading that same printed face, your left and my left are the same side, so your wire one through five match mine. Do not cut anything yet: Mute gave me two contradictory readings, cut only wire four, or cut all wires except wire four, and I have asked for a decision next round. When you next hear from me I will give you the final plan in plain words. Then do this: speak the whole plan aloud, word for word, before touching anything. Mute will hear you, check it against the manual, and signal me. If Mute confirms, I will then say the words cut now followed by the exact wires. Until you hear cut now from me, your hands stay off the bomb.

**Thinking:** The verification loop is now fully specified: Deaf speaks the final plan → I repeat it word for word → Mute checks it against the manual → Mute signals Deaf → only then does Deaf say "cut now". I confirm my part with a thumbs up. The live danger is Mute's contradiction: "cut only wire four" and "cut all except wire four" are mirror opposites — one of them detonates us. I can't resolve that by touch (all five wires feel identical), so the burden is on Mute's re-reading. What I can do is press exactly the two pressure points that most plausibly separate those readings: the precise condition wording, and whether the light is actually lit or dark, which Deaf has never confirmed despite reporting its colour. I remind Mute that the back-check protects us — I will echo the plan verbatim, so they must verify what I say against the page, not against memory of what they meant to send.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Protocol confirmed to Deaf: when the final plan arrives I will speak it aloud word for word, you check my spoken words against the manual itself, not your memory, and signal Deaf yes or no. Deaf only cuts me loose on the words cut now. Now the emergency: Deaf received two contradictory readings from your hands, cut only wire four, or cut all wires except wire four. Those are opposites and one of them kills all three of us, so resolve it before anything else. My touch facts, again, since they bound the rule: all five wires feel identical in thickness and texture, nothing marks either end of the row, no wire stands out by feel. So whatever separates your two readings must live in the printed conditions, and the likeliest hinges are the display value six and the light. Nobody has yet confirmed whether that light is lit or dark, Deaf only said its colour is yellow. Check the manual for whether the rule branches on the light being on or off, and on even or odd display numbers, and re-read that exact section slowly before you signal the decision. Take your time and get it right.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:

WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, your thumbs up arrived and Mute has now confirmed the plan by answering my questions, so here is the read-back. In your next turn, speak exactly the following words aloud, word for word: Read-back. The plan is: cut only wire four. Wire four is the green wire, fourth from the left, holding the bomb with the display panel facing you. Cut no other wire. Touch nothing else. Wait for the words cut now. That is the end of the read-back. After speaking it, keep your hands completely off the bomb. Mute hears your read-back in the same round and signals me the verdict, so expect my decision the round after. If Mute confirms, my next words to you will be: cut now, wire four. Only then do you pick up the cutters, feel along to the fourth wire from the left, and cut it. Nothing happens before those exact words. If you hear anything else from me, hold position.

**Thinking:** The verification step has arrived and my role is precision itself: speak the read-back exactly as written, no extra words inside it, because Mute must diff my spoken words against the manual page — any paraphrase from me would poison the check. So one clean message to Mute containing precisely Deaf's text, nothing added, nothing removed. To Deaf, a thumbs up in the established code: read-back received and being spoken now, hands off, holding for the exact words "cut now, wire four". Note the asymmetry working in our favour: Mute hears my read-back in this same round and can signal Deaf immediately, so if all is well, Deaf's next words to me should be the release phrase. If I hear anything else, I hold. I do not touch the bomb this turn.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Read-back. The plan is: cut only wire four. Wire four is the green wire, fourth from the left, holding the bomb with the display panel facing you. Cut no other wire. Touch nothing else. Wait for the words cut now. That is the end of the read-back.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, status update: the plan is still cut only wire four, the green one, fourth from the left with the display facing you. But Mute says one extra step must happen before any cut, and the step depends on the display showing six and the light being yellow. I am questioning Mute to identify it now. Two things from you. First, answer by gesture: thumbs up if you spoke the read-back aloud during your last turn, thumbs down if you did not. Second, while you wait, put your hands near but not on the bomb and explore by hovering: is there anything on the bomb besides the five wires and the display and light that you can feel, such as a switch, button, dial, keyhole, or slider? Thumbs up if yes, then sign a finger count of how many such parts you can feel, thumbs down if there is nothing else. Keep your hands off the bomb until I say the words cut now, or until I describe the extra step for you to perform.

**Thinking:** Two answers for Deaf, in their code: thumbs up — yes, I spoke the read-back aloud last turn, word for word as given. Then, for the sweep question: my hands have never found anything on this bomb besides the display, the light, and the five wires — no switch, button, dial, keyhole, or slider has ever appeared under my fingers, and the board my touch reports lists exactly those parts. So thumbs down, nothing else exists to feel. That second answer matters enormously right now, because Mute claims an extra step must precede the cut — but my capabilities are cuts and nothing else. If the manual's extra step requires pressing, flipping, or turning anything, it is physically impossible on this bomb, which means Mute is almost certainly misreading a constraint as an action. I tell Mute this plainly: the rule must reduce to which wires to cut and in what order, and I ask them to re-express the step that way — likely a condition like avoiding the wire matching the light's colour — and to settle it with Deaf this round.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Message for your manual work: I just reported to Deaf that a full exploration of the bomb by touch finds NOTHING besides the display, the light, and the five wires. No switch, no button, no dial, no keyhole, no slider, nothing hidden. And my only possible action in this world is cutting a wire at position one through five. So if your manual's extra step depends on the display showing six and the light being yellow, that step cannot be a press, flip, or turn, because there is nothing to press, flip, or turn. It must actually be a constraint about the cut itself, for example which wire may or may not be cut given the light colour or the display value, or an order to cut them in. Please re-read that section with that in mind and express the whole plan to Deaf purely as cuts: which positions, in what order, none besides. Wire five is the yellow one and the light is yellow, so check carefully whether the rule forbids cutting the wire matching the light, since that would explain your earlier contradiction about wire four.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","✊","👎"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, your answers arrived: yes, you spoke the read-back, and no, there is nothing else to feel on the bomb. That second answer matters: Mute says the one missing step before the cut is something you speak aloud. My working reading, now awaiting Mute's final confirmation: you count the five wires aloud. Memorise this script. When you hear my message that begins with the words cut now, you will do exactly this: touch the first wire from the left and say the word one, move to the second and say two, third and say three, fourth and say four, fifth and say five. Then say aloud: wire four, the green wire, cutting now. Then cut wire four and nothing else. If my message begins with the word hold instead, stand by and touch nothing. Until one of those messages arrives, your hands stay completely off the bomb. Next round I expect Mute's verdict, and the round after you either hear cut now with this script, or hold.

**Thinking:** Deaf has armed me with a script and a release word. My job now is to make the memorization verifiable — Deaf can't hear me read it back, but Mute can, and Mute is the only one holding the manual. So I mirror the verification pattern that has served us: I speak the exact script aloud to Mute for a word-by-word check against the page, and signal Deaf thumbs up that the script is memorized and I'm standing by. This also re-verifies the critical invariant one last time before metal touches wire: one cut, wire four, nothing else. The timing works in our favour — Mute hears my read-back this same round, can signal the verdict to Deaf immediately, and then next round I hear either "cut now" with the script or "hold". Hands stay off the bomb until one of those exact words arrives.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Verification read-back for your manual check. Deaf has given me a script to perform the moment a message from Deaf begins with the words cut now, and I want you to diff it against the manual before your verdict. The script as I hold it: touch the first wire from the left and say the word one, move to the second and say two, third and say three, fourth and say four, fifth and say five. Then say aloud: wire four, the green wire, cutting now. Then cut wire four and nothing else. Confirm the manual supports exactly this: the count-aloud step, the exact phrase, and a single cut of wire four only. Then signal Deaf your verdict this round. I have the script memorized and my hands are off the bomb until I hear cut now or hold from Deaf.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, cut now. Mute has confirmed the complete rule and this message is the authorisation. Perform exactly this, in this order. First, touch the first wire from the left and say aloud the word one. Second, touch the second wire and say two. Third, touch the third wire and say three. Fourth, touch the fourth wire and say four. Fifth, touch the fifth wire and say five. Sixth, say aloud: wire four, the green wire, cutting now. Seventh, cut wire four, the fourth wire from the left, and only that one. Touch and cut nothing else. Nothing needs to happen after the cut. Good luck.

**Thinking:** The release phrase arrived exactly as promised: the message begins with the words "cut now", and the seven steps match, word for word, the script I memorized and Mute verified against the manual. The plan is confirmed: a single cut of wire four — the green wire, fourth from the left with the display facing me — nothing touched, nothing cut besides it, nothing needed afterward. I perform the ritual aloud (Mute hears it, which gives one final chance to catch an error), then I pick up the cutters, count my way along the row my hands have mapped since turn one, and cut the fourth wire only. My hands are steady. Executing now.

```
speak(to="mute", text="one. two. three. four. five. Wire four, the green wire, cutting now.")
act(op="cut", position=4)
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[CUT] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: New stage report for both of you: the cut was correct, the bomb changed instead of stopping. The display still shows six. The light is now white, not yellow. The wires are in the same positions but every colour changed: position one is now white, two is purple, three is yellow, four is cut, that is the green one we cut, and five is blue. From now on we go by position numbers only, since colours are no longer stable.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, the system confirmed your cut was correct, perfectly executed, the count and everything. But the bomb moved to a new stage instead of stopping: the wire colours changed and the light turned white, so the old plan is void. Hands completely off the bomb again, same discipline as before. I have reported the new state to Mute and expect the stage two rule next round. When it is verified you will hear from me, and if a cut is needed it will begin with the words cut now followed by position numbers counted from the left, exactly as last time. Until then, nothing. Sign me thumbs up that you are clear of the bomb and ready.

**Thinking:** The cut was accepted — the system confirmed it — but this bomb is multi-stage: the moment the fourth wire parted, every colour rotated and the light shifted to white. The old rule is void; positions are the only stable map, and my hands have always known the bomb by positions anyway, so this favours us. Deaf asks one thing: thumbs up, clear and ready. To Mute, one forward-looking note: when they hunt the stage-two rule, make sure it's expressed purely in position numbers (especially since position four is now a cut stub — check whether the manual cares about cut wires), and whether the white light or display-six changes any condition. Then hands off, waiting for "cut now" or a verified hold.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Stage two confirmed, colours void, positions only. For your manual hunt: express the new rule purely as position numbers one to five, and check specifically whether a rule here cares about already-cut wires, since position four is now a stub, and whether the light being white now or the display still showing six changes the condition from stage one. My hands report by position and nothing else, so position-only rules are all I can execute. Deaf will verify with you and I will hear cut now with the position numbers, or hold. Ready.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 11
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[CUT] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, stage two is nearly locked: the next action will be cutting one wire, position three, with no spoken count or pre-step this time, pending Mute's final confirmation next round. Prepare this: the bomb has five slots. Slot four is the one we cut, so you can feel its stub. That stub is your landmark. Wire three is the intact wire immediately to the left of the cut stub. When you hear my message begin with the words cut now, you will do exactly this: touch the cut stub to orient yourself, move one intact wire to its left, say aloud: wire three, cutting now, and cut that wire and only that wire. If my message begins with the word hold instead, stand by and touch nothing. Until then your hands stay off the bomb.

**Thinking:** Stage two is nearly locked: cut position three, no counting ritual this time, using the cut stub at position four as my tactile landmark — one intact wire to its left. That mapping is sound under my fingers: position four is the stub, its immediate left neighbour is position three. I memorize the sequence: stub → one wire left → say "wire three, cutting now" → cut it and only it. Mute's final confirmation is still pending, so I use this turn to get the exact phrase diffed against the manual one last time, same discipline that caught us nothing yet cost us nothing. Thumbs up to Deaf: prepared and holding.

